question: Users are repeatedly redirected to sign-in after the SSO change
author: Sarah Connor

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: I reproduced successful authentication followed by another login redirect. It happens consistently in the test environment.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: I compared cookie attributes between environments. The observations match the original report.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: Additional testing shows the problem affecting only the new identity provider, while the control scenario completes normally.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: The logs point toward this cause: the session cookie is marked SameSite=Strict and is dropped during the cross-site identity-provider callback.

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: Can someone verify this with another affected account before we change the configuration?

resolution: Set the authentication cookie to SameSite=None with Secure enabled and retest the SSO callback flow.

question: Case details take more than ten seconds to open
author: Elena Garcia

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: I reproduced slow record loading. It happens consistently in the test environment.

replies.author: Nisha Rao
replies.text: I measured the JSON aggregation query. The observations match the original report.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: Additional testing shows performance worsening as work-note count grows, while the control scenario completes normally.

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: The logs point toward this cause: the endpoint loads and serializes every historical work note even though the UI initially shows only the latest entries.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Can someone verify this with another affected account before we change the configuration?

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: Confirmed with a second account. I also tested the same record without its work notes, and the same pattern is present.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: A temporary workaround is available, but it should not replace the permanent correction.

resolution: Paginate work notes, fetch the initial page separately and add an index supporting the note ordering.

question: Report download stops at ten thousand records
author: Daniel Kim

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: I reproduced the preview count exceeding the exported row count. It happens consistently in the test environment.

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: I reviewed export pagination logs. The observations match the original report.

replies.author: Nisha Rao
replies.text: Additional testing shows no visible error during download, while the control scenario completes normally.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: The logs point toward this cause: the export worker stops after the default pagination limit instead of requesting all result pages.

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: Can someone verify this with another affected account before we change the configuration?

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Confirmed with a second account. I also tested several result sizes, and the same pattern is present.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: A temporary workaround is available, but it should not replace the permanent correction.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: The proposed fix is ready in the test environment. The previously failing scenario now succeeds.

resolution: Process every page with a continuation token and stream the CSV so large exports do not exhaust memory.

question: Mobile users cannot submit a case when the description is long
author: Aarav Mehta

replies.author: Nisha Rao
replies.text: I reproduced the submit button remaining disabled. It happens consistently in the test environment.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: I compared mobile and desktop validation. The observations match the original report.

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: Additional testing shows desktop submission working with the same text, while the control scenario completes normally.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: The logs point toward this cause: the mobile validator counts UTF-16 units differently from the backend character limit.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: Can someone verify this with another affected account before we change the configuration?

resolution: Use the same Unicode-aware character-counting rule in mobile and backend validation.
